_readme: How mChatAI+ recognises 'this CLI is not signed in' in a backend's own error text, and what to do about it. CONTENT, not binary: these strings are written by third parties (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) and change on THEIR release cycle, not ours — a list baked into the app is wrong the day a vendor rewords a message, and a shipped user cannot recompile. Edit by PR; refreshMchataisourceCache picks it up with no rebuild.
_consumer: mChatAI+ CLIAuthFailureDetector -> WorkbenchController.authFailures -> the Workbench sign-in card
_failure_mode: If this file is missing or unparseable, NOTHING is classified and the raw CLI line is shown exactly as before. Degrading to the old behaviour is safe; inventing a second copy of these patterns inside the binary is not (ABSOLUTE RULE #1).

claude.guidance: Claude Code's sign-in expired. This is the CLI's own login on this Mac — nothing to do with the sites you are browsing, or with your mChatAI+ account.
claude.afterAction: A terminal opens here and runs /login. Claude Code will hand you a link to finish in the browser, then you can resume the conversation.

codex.guidance: The Codex CLI is not signed in on this Mac. This is its own login, separate from your mChatAI+ account and from anything you are browsing.
codex.afterAction: A terminal opens here and starts the login. Finish it in the browser, then resume the conversation.

gemini.guidance: The Gemini CLI's credentials have expired on this Mac. This is its own login, separate from your mChatAI+ account.
gemini.afterAction: A terminal opens here and starts re-authentication. Finish it in the browser, then resume the conversation.
